steps: Scaffold an Express project with TypeScript inside an `api/` directory; configure `tsconfig.json`, `nodemon` for development restarts, and a `build` script that compiles to `dist/`
Load environment variables with `dotenv` for DATABASE_URL, PORT, UPLOAD_DIR, and CLAUDE_MODEL; provide a committed `.env.example` listing every required variable
Add CORS middleware allowing the local Vite dev origin and configure it to restrict origins in production via an env variable
Mount a `GET /health` endpoint that returns `{ status: 'ok', timestamp }` and the server version so deploy pipelines can verify liveness
Add `morgan` or `pino` for structured HTTP request logging; verify the server starts cleanly on the configured port with a startup log line

description: Set up PostgreSQL database schema and migrations
steps: Configure a `pg` connection pool using `DATABASE_URL`; use `node-pg-migrate` (or `knex`) as the migration runner and wire a `npm run migrate` script
Create the `categories` table: `id` (serial PK), `name` (text, unique, not null), `color` (text, hex code), `icon` (text, optional emoji/slug), `created_at` (timestamptz default now)

Create the `movements` table: `id` (serial PK), `amount` (numeric(12,2), not null), `date` (date, not null), `description` (text), `store` (text), `category_id` (FK → categories, nullable), `created_at` / `updated_at` (timestamptz)

Create the `attachments` table: `id` (serial PK), `movement_id` (FK → movements, nullable — null before import confirmation), `file_name` (text), `file_path` (text), `mime_type` (text), `created_at` (timestamptz)
Add a seed migration that inserts default categories: Food, Transport, Entertainment, Health, Utilities, Shopping, Other — each with a distinct color
`GET /api/categories` — return all categories ordered by name, each with a `movement_count` computed via a left join
`POST /api/categories` — create a category; validate `name` (required, unique) and `color` (optional, must be a valid hex string if provided)
`PUT /api/categories/:id` — update name, color, or icon; re-validate uniqueness excluding the current row
`DELETE /api/categories/:id` — reject with 409 if any movement references the category; otherwise hard-delete and return 204
Return a consistent error shape `{ error: string, details?: Record<string, string> }` for all validation failures and use appropriate HTTP status codes throughout

description: Implement the expense movements REST API
steps: `GET /api/movements` — accept filter query params (`from`, `to` date range; `category_id`; `store`; `search` for description/store full-text); return paginated results (`page`, `limit`) with `total` count and each movement's attached files
`GET /api/movements/:id` — return a single movement joined with its category and its attachments array
`POST /api/movements` — create a movement; validate `amount` (positive number) and `date` (ISO date string, defaults to today if omitted); `category_id`, `description`, and `store` are optional
`PUT /api/movements/:id` — update any movement field; re-validate the same rules as POST
`DELETE /api/movements/:id` — delete the movement, its attachment records, and each attachment file from disk; return 204

description: Handle file attachment uploads and serving
steps: Configure `multer` with a disk storage engine that saves files under `UPLOAD_DIR/<YYYY-MM>/`; restrict accepted MIME types to `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/webp`, and `application/pdf`; cap individual file size at 10 MB
`POST /api/attachments` — accept a multipart upload with `file` and an optional `movement_id`; persist a row to `attachments` and return the created record including a public URL
`DELETE /api/attachments/:id` — remove the DB row and delete the file from disk; return 204
Mount a static route so uploaded files are accessible at `GET /uploads/<relative-path>` with correct `Content-Type` headers
Return a 400 with a human-readable message for unsupported file types or size-exceeded errors; never leave orphan files on disk when a DB insert fails

description: Suggest a matching category for a movement using AI
steps: Add `POST /api/suggest/category` — accept `{ store?, description? }` (at least one field required); return 400 with a clear message if both are absent

Fetch all categories from the DB, then call the OpenRouter chat completions endpoint via the `openai` npm package (baseURL `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`, key from `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`) passing the store name, description, and the full category list; use `response_format: { type: 'json_object' }` and prompt the model to return `{ categoryId: number | null, reason: string }` — `null` when no category fits well

Use the model name from `OPENROUTER_MODEL` env var (default: `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`) with a hard timeout of 3 seconds and `temperature: 0` for deterministic output; on timeout or unparseable JSON return `{ categoryId: null }` without throwing — the caller must never be blocked

Return `{ categoryId, categoryName, color }` sourced from the matched DB row so the frontend can update the select without a second round-trip; return `{ categoryId: null }` when the model finds no confident match
Extract a shared `suggestCategory(store, description)` helper function from this handler so it can be called internally (e.g. from the OCR extraction pipeline) without an extra HTTP hop

description: Extract expense data from images using OCR and AI
steps: `POST /api/import/extract` — accept a single image upload (JPEG, PNG, PDF); save it as a temporary attachment row with `movement_id = null`
Run `tesseract` CLI (via `child_process.execFile`) on the uploaded image with the `eng` language model to produce raw extracted text; surface a clear error if `tesseract` is not installed

Build a structured prompt containing the raw OCR text and call the OpenRouter chat completions endpoint (same `openai` client used by the category suggester) requesting a JSON array of movement objects: `{ amount, date, description, store }`; use `OPENROUTER_MODEL` with `response_format: { type: 'json_object' }` and a short timeout

After parsing the movements array, call the shared `suggestCategory(store, description)` helper for each movement in parallel; attach the resolved `{ categoryId, categoryName, color, aiSuggested: true }` to each movement object before returning

Return the response payload `{ attachmentId, rawText, movements: [...] }` to the caller; if Claude is unavailable or returns unparseable JSON, return `{ attachmentId, rawText, movements: [], error: 'AI extraction failed' }` so the UI can fall back to manual entry; never persist movement rows at this stage

description: Import preview confirmation: bulk-create reviewed movements
steps: `POST /api/import/confirm` — accept `{ attachmentId, movements: [...] }` where `movements` is the user-reviewed array of movement objects
Validate every movement in the array (amount positive, date valid, category_id exists if provided) before persisting any; return per-item errors if validation fails without creating anything
Insert all movements in a single database transaction; link `attachmentId` to each created movement by setting `movement_id` on the attachment row
Return `{ created: [{ id, amount, date, description }], count: N }` on success so the UI can navigate to the newly created records
If `attachmentId` is not provided or the attachment row is not found, still proceed with movement creation but skip the attachment link step

description: Provide aggregate data API for dashboard charts
steps: `GET /api/dashboard` — accept `period` (day | week | month | year | all) and optional `anchor` (ISO date, defaults to today); compute the inclusive date range for the requested period

Return `{ totalAmount, movementCount, categoryBreakdown: [{ categoryId, name, color, total, percentage }], timeSeries: [{ label, total }] }` where `timeSeries` buckets are hours for day, days for week/month, and months for year/all
Compute all aggregates in a single PostgreSQL query using `DATE_TRUNC` and `GROUP BY` to avoid N+1 queries; include empty buckets (zero-amount) so charts render continuous axes
Include `previousPeriod: { totalAmount, movementCount }` for the preceding equivalent range so the frontend can render trend deltas
Return `topStore` (the store with the highest spend in the period) alongside the aggregates
Scaffold a React + TypeScript project with Vite inside a `client/` directory; configure the Vite dev server to proxy `/api` and `/uploads` requests to the Express server port
Add Tailwind CSS with a custom color palette that includes tokens for primary, success, warning, danger, and neutral scales; configure dark-mode support via the `class` strategy
Set up React Router v6 with routes for `/` (Dashboard), `/import` (OCR Import), and `/categories` (Category Management); add a persistent top navigation bar with links to each route

Add `axios` (or `fetch`-based) API client utilities organized by resource (`movements`, `categories`, `dashboard`, `import`) with shared error handling that surfaces API `error` payloads as typed exceptions

Configure ESLint and Prettier to match the API project; add a root-level `package.json` with scripts: `dev` (runs API + Vite concurrently), `build` (Vite build + API tsc), `start` (production Express serving the React build), `migrate`

description: Build the dashboard page with expense summary and charts
steps: Lay out a summary row at the top showing three stat cards: Total Spend, Number of Movements, and Top Category — each with a label, formatted value, and a trend indicator (▲/▼ vs. the previous period)

Render a donut/pie chart of spend by category using Recharts; display the category name, color swatch, total, and percentage in a legend beside the chart; show a 'No data' illustration when the period has no movements

Render a bar chart of spend over time (sub-period buckets returned by the dashboard API) below the donut; label the x-axis with readable date labels appropriate to the period (e.g. 'Mon', 'Jan 5', 'Feb')
Show a 'Recent Movements' list below the charts with columns: date, store/description, category badge, and amount; link each row to open an edit form
Show skeleton loaders while data is fetching; show a full-page empty state with a call-to-action to add the first movement when there are no records at all

description: Add a time period selector to the dashboard
steps: Render a segmented control (tab strip) with five options: Day | Week | Month | Year | All; default to Month on first load
For Day, Week, Month, and Year periods render previous/next arrow buttons flanking a human-readable label (e.g. 'June 2026', 'Week of Jun 2–8', 'Monday Jun 9'); the All period hides the arrows
Clicking a period segment or the prev/next arrows updates the `period` and `anchor` URL query params; the component reads them on mount so the URL is bookmarkable
Debounce rapid prev/next clicks (e.g. 150 ms) to avoid flooding the API; show an inline spinner on the stat cards while the new period is loading without clearing the previous chart data
Disable the 'next' arrow when the anchor would advance past today

description: Build the expense movement registration form
steps: Open a slide-over panel or modal from a prominent '+ Add Expense' button fixed to the top-right of the dashboard; the panel should not navigate away from the current view

Form fields: Amount (number input, required, formatted with locale currency), Date (date picker defaulting to today, required, editable), Description (text), Store (text), Category (select populated from GET /api/categories with a colored badge per option), Attachments (multi-file input accepting images and PDFs)

After the user types or blurs from the Store or Description field, fire a debounced call (400 ms) to `POST /api/suggest/category`; while the request is in flight show a subtle spinner icon inside the Category select; on response pre-select the returned category and display a small ✦ 'AI suggested' badge beside the select label — the user can always override by picking a different option, which clears the badge
On submit, POST the movement fields to `/api/movements`, then POST each selected file to `/api/attachments` with the returned `movement_id`; show a per-file upload progress indicator

Display inline field-level validation errors (missing amount, invalid date, etc.) before the network call; show a success toast and close the panel on completion; show an error toast if the API returns an error

Support editing an existing movement: pre-populate all fields from the movement record, show existing attachments as thumbnails with a remove button (calls DELETE /api/attachments/:id), and PATCH the movement on save

description: Build the OCR-assisted image import flow
steps: Step 1 — Upload: at `/import`, render a centered drop zone that accepts drag-and-drop or click-to-browse for a single JPEG, PNG, or PDF file; show a thumbnail preview after selection and a 'Process Image' button

Step 2 — Processing: on clicking 'Process Image', POST to `/api/import/extract`; display a multi-stage progress indicator ('Extracting text…', 'Analyzing with AI…') and show the raw extracted text in a collapsible panel for debugging

Step 3 — Review: render an editable table of extracted movements — one row per movement with inline-editable cells for Amount, Date, Description, Store, and Category (select); Category cells that were pre-filled by AI show a ✦ 'AI suggested' badge; changing Store or Description in a row fires the same debounced `POST /api/suggest/category` call used by the manual form, updating the suggestion in real time; allow adding blank rows and removing any row; show the uploaded image in a side panel so the user can cross-check
Step 4 — Confirm: a 'Import N Movements' button posts the reviewed array to `/api/import/confirm`; on success show a summary card listing each created movement with a link to view it on the dashboard

Error handling: if extraction fails (OCR error or AI unavailable), display the raw text with a notice explaining the AI could not parse it, and let the user fill in movements manually before confirming
At `/categories`, render a list of all categories; each row shows a color swatch, name, icon (if set), and movement count badge

Provide an 'Add Category' inline form at the top of the list: a text input for name, a color picker (a palette of preset hex colors plus a native `<input type=color>`), and an optional emoji input; submit calls POST /api/categories
Allow editing a category's name, color, and icon in-place by clicking an edit icon on the row; save on blur or Enter key

Show a delete icon on each row; clicking it opens a small confirmation popover; if movements are linked, disable the delete icon and show a tooltip with the movement count explaining why deletion is blocked
Show an empty state illustration with a 'Create your first category' prompt when the list is empty

description: Containerize the application with Docker and Docker Compose
steps: Write a multi-stage `api/Dockerfile`: a `builder` stage that installs all deps and compiles TypeScript to `dist/`, and a lean `runtime` stage (node:lts-slim) that installs `tesseract-ocr` and the `eng` language pack via apt, copies only `dist/` and production `node_modules`, and sets the `CMD` to `node dist/index.js`

Write a multi-stage `client/Dockerfile`: a `builder` stage that runs `vite build`, and a `runtime` stage based on `nginx:alpine` that copies the built `dist/` into `/usr/share/nginx/html` and adds an `nginx.conf` that serves the SPA with a `try_files` fallback to `index.html`

Write a `docker-compose.yml` at the repo root with three services: `postgres` (official `postgres:16-alpine` image, named volume `pgdata` for `/var/lib/postgresql/data`, healthcheck using `pg_isready`), `api` (built from `api/Dockerfile`, depends_on postgres with condition `service_healthy`, named volume `uploads` mounted at `UPLOAD_DIR`, env vars sourced from `.env`), and `client` (built from `client/Dockerfile`, depends_on api, exposes port 80)

Write a `docker-compose.override.yml` for local development: override the `api` service to mount `./api/src` into the container and run `nodemon` for hot-reload; override the `client` service to run `vite --host` with `./client/src` mounted instead of building the static image; expose the Vite dev port (5173) directly

Add `.dockerignore` files in both `api/` and `client/` excluding `node_modules`, `.env`, `dist/`, and test artefacts; document the full dev workflow in the README: `cp .env.example .env`, `docker compose up --build`, then `docker compose run api npm run migrate`

description: Cross-cutting: validation, error handling, and production configuration
steps: Use `zod` (or `express-validator`) on every POST and PUT endpoint to validate request bodies; on failure return 400 with `{ error: 'Validation failed', details: { field: message } }`

Add a global Express error handler that catches unhandled errors, logs the stack trace via the configured logger, and returns 500 with `{ error: 'Internal server error' }` without leaking stack traces in production

In production mode (`NODE_ENV=production`), the Express container serves only the API; the `client` nginx container handles static file serving and SPA routing — ensure the nginx `location /api` block proxies to the `api` service hostname

Add a `.env.example` at the repo root documenting every variable consumed by `docker-compose.yml`: `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `POSTGRES_DB`, `DATABASE_URL`, `PORT` (default 3000), `UPLOAD_DIR` (default `/app/uploads`), `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (set in shell via `~/.zshrc`, copy value from `$OPENROUTER_API_KEY`), `OPENROUTER_MODEL` (default `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`), `NODE_ENV`; add `.env` to `.gitignore` so the key is never committed

Add a root-level README section covering both Docker and bare-metal workflows: Docker path is `cp .env.example .env && docker compose up --build && docker compose run api npm run migrate`; bare-metal path is install deps, set env vars, `npm run migrate`, `npm run dev`
